newsitem.title: UK: Most LME metals end softer, lead tests upside.
newsitem.headline: Most LME metals end softer, lead tests upside.

text.p: Most LME metals consolidated at slightly weaker levels on Tuesday afternoon, taking a well-earned breather, but lead ticked higher.
Many metals needed to correct after strong gains over the last few weeks, but found limited scope on the downside.
"We've seen very good support under the market. None of them have really damaged their uptrends," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
Three months lead dipped to $696 per tonne, but in the afternoon clawed its way back to Monday's high of $710, finishing $4 higher at $708.
"The tightness developing in April and May is lending support to the market...but it really needs to get above $710. It has some more work to do," Squires said.
The premium of cash over three months metal firmed slightly to $7/$10, up $3 from Monday.
Further resistance was pegged at $726 based on a trendline, $730 and $758, Squires said.
All of the other metals ended in negative territory.
Auminium, hit by fund and speculative liquidation, despite a hefty stocks fall of 6,100 tonnes, ended $26 weaker at $1,642, only $2 above its low.
Below $1,640, support was pegged at $1,634 and $1,625.
The market has seen modest forward and trade buying, but further tests of the downside were likely as funds locked in their profits, traders said.
Copper finished at $2,333, off $12, and like aluminium, only slightly above its low of the day.
So far the $2,330 support has held and after a stocks decline of 3,800 tonnes, many traders were unsure of the next direction.
The premium of cash over three months eased to $40/$44, down $3/$4 from Monday.
Zinc slid further, correcting after touching a fresh 4-1/2 year peak of $1,307 on Monday.
Trade buying came in around lows of $1,286 and prices finished at $1,290, down $6.
Nickel dropped to $7,855 under pressure from fund and Chinese selling, but managed to pare the losses to close at $7,905, down $135.
Tin finished off $25 at $6,030 and alloy ended weaker at $1,530/35 compared to $1,545.
